analysis.investment_thesis: Apollo Techno screens decently on return on capital (ROCE 31%) but the earnings yield is mediocre (~9% EBIT/EV at EV/EBITDA 11.2x), so it fails the "cheap AND good" Magic Formula test. The FY25 EBIT jump from INR 8 Cr to INR 18 Cr looks like a one-time inflection that needs durability proof before it earns a buy.
key_strengths: ROCE 31.2% — clears the >20% Magic Formula bar on capital efficiency.
Operating leverage kicking in: EBIT CAGR 56% (FY21-25) on revenue CAGR 20%.
FCF turned positive last two years (INR 13 Cr, INR 15 Cr) with negligible capex.
key_risks: Earnings yield only ~9% (EBIT 18 / EV ~201 Cr) — not cheap enough for the formula.
D/E of 1.16 inflates the headline 73.8% ROE; one bad year compresses both metrics.
FY25 margin step-up (Op margin 3% → 18%) is unproven; could mean-revert.
red_flags: Net profit base is tiny and erratic (INR 0 Cr in FY21–22 to INR 14 Cr in FY25).
Cash balance reported as ~0 despite INR 32 Cr debt — liquidity is thin.
Newly listed micro-cap (incorporated 2016) with no FII participation and only ~12% DII.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying the Magic Formula: Earnings Yield = EBIT INR 18 Cr / EV ~INR 201 Cr (implied by EV/EBITDA 11.19) ≈ 9%, which is below my 12% attractiveness threshold. Return on Capital using EBIT / (Equity INR 29 Cr + Debt INR 32 Cr) ≈ 30%, which is genuinely good and consistent with the reported ROCE of 31.2%. So this is a "good but not cheap" stock — exactly the kind that ranks in the middle of the formula and shouldn't be a top pick.

The bigger issue is sustainability. EBIT was INR 2-3 Cr from FY21-23, then INR 8 Cr in FY24, then INR 18 Cr in FY25 — a 6x jump in two years on revenue that only grew ~40%. That looks like a cyclical infra/order-book tailwind (HDD rigs, metro/airport diaphragm wall demand) rather than a structural moat. Combined with 1.16x D/E, near-zero cash, and a tiny INR ~155 Cr market cap, this is a speculative micro-cap, not a systematic Magic Formula buy. I'd want to see two more years of INR 15+ Cr EBIT before paying ~11x earnings for it.
